fact: Chapter 2 is titled 'Functions Of The Mind' and its epigraph is Ecclesiastes 10:18, 'By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through'
Anything that is not put to use will become disused and will soon cease to function
The building analogy: any building not put to use soon begins to run down, and it runs down FASTER than a building that is fully in use
In like manner your mind has specific tasks that it carries out, and if not put to use it will run down
To keep the mind in top form you ask yourself what the fundamental functions of your mind are, so you can keep it alive and not watch it run down
The author outlines FOUR major functions of the mind, and your mind will be productive if fully engaged in them
The four functions of the mind, named together at the close of the chapter, are learning, understanding, reasoning and imagination
If your mind is fully utilized in carrying out the four functions then you will be set for your high place on the earth
Learning is the first function of the mind, and learning takes place in the mind
The mind is able to acquire and store information, making it available for use when it is required
Dr. T. L. Osborn said 'When you stop learning, you start dying', and the author says he totally agrees with it
Abraham Lincoln said 'When you stop learning, you're old, whether at 20 or 80'
Your age is not what determines old age
If your mind is not put to proper use your body soon begins to age; if you keep your mind young by putting it to proper use, it will youngen your body
The great task before you is to keep your mind alive through a consistent learning process so you do not become outdated
Be conscious of the need to be current, and be open to learn
The largest room in the world, we are told, is the room for improvement
Daniel was the wisest man in his time, and Daniel 9:2 records 'I Daniel understood by books...'
Even though Daniel was the master of astrologers, magicians, Chaldeans and soothsayers, he was still a learner
People start ageing from the mind, not the body, which is why when you stop learning you start dying
When your mind starts becoming outdated your body also starts ageing, but if any man keeps learning he remains young

The author has written some books on wisdom but still has plenty of books by other authors that he consults with delight on the subject, learning from them things he did not know when he was writing his own
There are people today who since they left school have never read one whole book: all they do is read the conclusion and probably the introduction, and then close the book
Anthony Robbins is reported to have read 700 books in his high school days, ranging from Psychology to Philosophy and various other subjects
Anthony Robbins grew to become a man of solutions in his school, so much so that even his teachers began consulting him
Anthony Robbins finished high school and became an instant celebrity, having exercised his senses through learning
Anthony Robbins is now a consultant to IBM and to Presidents of many developed countries
The rebuke about unread books: you know the titles and authors, but you do not know the contents, and they are just there neatly arranged on your library shelf
Paul was one of the wisest men in his days

Peter said of Paul in 2 Peter 3:15-16, 'Even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you... speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood'
2 Timothy 4:13 records Paul instructing Timothy: 'The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments'
In asking for the parchments Paul was talking about his notes
Paul wrote about 50 per cent of the New Testament, yet he was still carrying books and notes about
Your mind will die except you put it to work
It was God who gave Paul wisdom, but Paul had to keep his mind alive by learning; God gave Daniel wisdom, yet Daniel had to consult books in order to acquire understanding
Learning culminates in knowledge, and knowledge is what you acquire in the process of learning
Knowledge is the sum or range of what has been perceived, discovered or learned
Knowledge is also the familiarity, awareness or understanding gained through experience or study
Knowledge is acquired through the use of the mind in learning
Knowledge is power, and John 8:32 is the scripture cited: 'ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free'
Hosea 4:6 is quoted: 'My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me...'
Knowledge is not just the art of gathering information, it is power, and it has the ability to set free
The mind is the principal tool in the learning process
A mad person cannot be in a class and gain anything from what is taught: you may force him to sit down, but you cannot force anything into him, because his mind is out of use
The mad person may be looking at the person speaking, but he does not have the ability to assimilate what is being taught, because his mind, which is the tool for acquiring knowledge, is out of use

From the parable of the talent we see that every divine deposit multiplies with use
Every businessman is told to learn by reading biographies of successful Christian businessmen, so that his business can come out of obscurity into the limelight
The local champion warning: do not die as a local champion who says 'My shop is the biggest on our street' when your street is nothing but an obscure place in an unknown area
The world is waiting to hear your name, so read books that will force you to think progress thoughts and to forge ahead
The author always reads books of those who are several times ahead of him, so that he can see his smallness and be determined to go forward
The author reads everything he can lay his hands on, to see if his brain can develop yet a little more
